=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh:234-237, 428-435 | severity=high | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The `cap_zero` early return in review_final_ci_sweep_base_sync (lines 234-237) and the `disabled` early return in review_final_ci_sweep_main (lines 428-435) both run before `_pr_base_sync_count` (line 252), so a head that already has the `ai:final-ci-stale-workflow:v1` marker never reaches review_final_ci_sweep_stale_hand_back.
  WHY: Pre-existing branches whose ci.yml lacks the new env lines (ci.yml lines 5256-5259) use the defaults in review_final_ci_failed.sh:154-159 (`FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_ENABLED:-true`, `FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_MAX:-3`), so the stale marker is posted anyway; the sweep then exits early on every tick, and the PR is left with a red final CI, no `ai:final-ci-failed:v1` marker, no review dispatch and no base sync. All five reviewers rated this MAJOR (mapped to high).
- scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh:213-216 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: review_final_ci_sweep_stale_hand_back runs `timeout 120 bash "${hand_back_dir}/review_final_ci_failed.sh" || true` and then always sets `FINAL_CI_SWEEP_STALE_NOTE=" stale_workflow=handed_back"`, whatever the hand-back did (read_failed, marker_failed, dispatch_failed, disabled, superseded, or a 120 s timeout).
  WHY: The contractual `REVIEW_FINAL_CI_BASE_SYNC` log line reports a hand-back that did not happen, and repeats it on every tick, so log analysis counts a stranded PR as handled. All five reviewers rated this NIT (mapped to low).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "When the update conflicts, the cap is reached, the files are equal, or the switch is off, the run is handed back to review as today." (issue #10093, Goals section)
  expected_change_site: scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh — the `disabled` exit in review_final_ci_sweep_main (lines 428-435) and the `cap_zero` exit in review_final_ci_sweep_base_sync (lines 234-237); tests/test_review_final_ci.py
  confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  EVIDENCE: Neither early exit calls `_pr_base_sync_count`, checks `PR_BASE_SYNC_STALE_WORKFLOW_MARKED`, or calls review_final_ci_sweep_stale_hand_back; all hand-back calls sit at or below line 252, after `_pr_base_sync_count`, the deferral-side defaults at scripts/review_final_ci_failed.sh:154-159 cannot cover pre-existing branches whose ci.yml lacks the new env exports, and tests/test_review_final_ci.py has no test of a stale-marked head with `FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_ENABLED=false` or `FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_MAX=0` at sweep time (the parametrized `switch_off` case in test_sweep_hands_a_stale_marked_head_back_when_it_cannot_sync only sets `FINAL_CI_STALE_WORKFLOW_SYNC_ENABLED=false`).
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh (with scripts/review_final_ci_failed.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml):review_final_ci_sweep.sh lines 428-435, 234-237, 252, 258-316; review_final_ci_failed.sh lines 154-159; ci.yml lines 5229-5231, 5256-5259 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The final-ci-failed job checks out the script from the default branch but takes its env from the head ref's ci.yml. Branches cut before this PR lack the new env lines, so the script falls back to its defaults and posts the ai:final-ci-stale-workflow:v1 marker. If vars.FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_ENABLED=false or vars.FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_MAX=0, the sweep returns at line 433 or line 236 and never reads the marker or calls the hand-back. The same is true of vars.FINAL_CI_STALE_WORKFLOW_SYNC_ENABLED=false, because the check at line 258 sits below both exits.
  WHY: The PR is left with a red final CI, no ai:final-ci-failed:v1 marker, no review dispatch and no base sync. `_pr_ensure_final_ci` keeps answering `exists failure`, so the PR stays stranded until someone pushes. This contradicts the issue goal and the README row. Suggested fix: in both branches, call `_pr_base_sync_count`, then call the hand-back when PR_BASE_SYNC_STALE_WORKFLOW_MARKED=true, and add tests for both settings.
- scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh:review_final_ci_sweep_stale_hand_back, lines 213-216 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `stale_workflow=handed_back` is set unconditionally after `timeout 120 bash "${hand_back_dir}/review_final_ci_failed.sh" || true`, whatever the script did (read_failed, marker_failed, dispatch_failed, disabled, superseded or a timeout). When the marker POST fails, the next tick repeats the hand-back and logs it again.
  WHY: REVIEW_FINAL_CI_BASE_SYNC is a contractual log prefix (agents.d/10093 fragment), so log analysis reports a stranded PR as handled. Suggested fix: capture stdout and set handed_back only on `outcome=redispatched|already_reported`, otherwise ` stale_workflow=hand_back_failed`.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "At most one such sync per head. When the update conflicts, the cap is reached, the files are equal, or the switch is off, the run is handed back to review as today."
  Expected change site: scripts/review_final_ci_sweep.sh: the `disabled` exit in review_final_ci_sweep_main (lines 428-435) and the `cap_zero` exit in review_final_ci_sweep_base_sync (lines 234-237). Also tests/test_review_final_ci.py.
  Evidence of absence: Neither exit hands a stale-marked head back; the hand-back calls are reached only after `_pr_base_sync_count` at line 252. The deferral gate (review_final_ci_failed.sh lines 154-159) cannot cover pre-existing branches. Every new sweep test runs with base sync enabled and a cap above 0.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- HARDENING_SUGGESTIONS (2 related items): capture the hand-back output in review_final_ci_sweep_stale_hand_back (lines 213-216, about 5 lines); add a stale-marker hand-back to the `disabled` branch (lines 428-435) and the `cap_zero` branch (lines 234-237), logged with reason base_sync_disabled or cap_zero (8-10 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

  WHY: If a head is already stale-marked and the configuration later changes, the PR stays stranded with a failed final CI and is never handed back to review. Every later tick exits early again.

  WHY: The `REVIEW_FINAL_CI_BASE_SYNC` log reports a hand-back that did not happen, which misleads log analysis.

  PROBLEM: The `cap_zero` return at line 234 and the `disabled` return at line 432 both run before the stale-workflow marker check at line 257. A PR that already carries `ai:final-ci-stale-workflow:v1` never reaches `review_final_ci_sweep_stale_hand_back`, so it gets no `ai:final-ci-failed:v1` marker and no review dispatch.
  WHY: review_final_ci_failed.sh lines 154-161 default to `FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_ENABLED:-true` and `FINAL_CI_SWEEP_BASE_SYNC_MAX:-3`. Pre-existing branches do not pass these envs, so the marker gets posted. If the operator then sets the cap to 0 or turns the switch off, the sweep cannot act on the marker.   WHY: On `marker_failed` the note still says handed back, so operators believe the PR was handed back when no marker was posted and no dispatch happened.
